scope: Kokoro word boundaries and decoded take durations for the two regression scenes. Both use scene-local time starting at zero.

changed.previousSay: Back in Ada’s live billing project, the question is which test she should use. Keep the replay receipt. Ada directly changed the verifier for this repository to the invoices test. The current profile now says version three. Search still has the billing test at version two. Ada still has access to this project. Which command belongs on the empty verifier line?

A project profile is usually a quick read. A search for supporting history can overlap it, up to the request’s time budget. If evidence hasn’t arrived, leave it out or ask for it on a later call. Check real return visits for missed receipts, stale or unauthorized records, prompt tokens and time to first token. A conversational benchmark only describes the cases it measured.

Ada can now see which event produced two invoices and which test to use today. In the run with an unknown outcome, her merge is still pending. Before sending anything, recovery has to check the destination and current approval for that exact change. That’s where the next lesson picks up.

beats.say: Let’s rewind to when Ada changed her test preference. In the article’s SQLite exercise, the host resolves source T three for the signed-in session, checks access and writes an index entry pointing to that source and version. That derived record is called a projection. Admission and storage happen inside one trusted service. Values go into the SQL as parameters. Close the database connection and reopen it. The source and index both say version one, and the read returns the old command.

Ada replaces the command with the billing test. The profile commits version two from her direct statement. Mark the earlier preference superseded and propagate the correction to summaries, search and caches. Keep your eye on the index. It still points to version one. Ada still has access and the record hasn’t expired. What will a read through that index return now?

It returns an empty list. The lookup joins on the source identity and requires the current version. That old index entry can’t supply the old value or the new one. Watch the index row. The worker commits version two to the index. Run the same read at the same time. This time it returns the billing command.

Keep both versions and Ada’s grant fixed. This record expires at second two hundred. Read it one second before expiry. The command still comes back. Advance the clock one second. Now the read returns an empty list. Both reads used the refreshed index. The source still sets the deadline.

Back at second one hundred and two, the index returns the billing command. Save that result in Ada’s prompt packet. Now mark the source deleted. Its tombstone keeps the identity, so even a late refresh can see the deletion. A fresh read comes back empty and the queued write is refused. Look at the packet we saved earlier. It still contains the command. Propagate deletion to summaries, caches and indexes. Already sent prompts, logs and backups have their own retention paths.

Here’s a separate check in the same exercise. Restore the test source and its index at version four. Both match. Take away Ada’s grant. The next read is empty again, and a refresh is denied. This local database tests persistence and read rules. The service in production must supply the authenticated session. A content hash can check the expected bytes. Authorship still needs a trusted source.

Ada changes one setting in her billing project. She wants the invoices test. The current profile now says version three. The search copy still has the billing test at version two. Which command belongs on the empty verifier line?

Skip the stale search copy and read Ada’s current project profile. Pin its invoices test in the next prompt. The application commits a direct preference before the turn that needs it. This prompt can use the scoped profile read as soon as it arrives. The summary and search index can catch up in the background.

The app can read the profile and search for related replays in parallel. Give the search a deadline. If it runs late, Ada can get her test command now and the extra history on a later call. On real return visits, track missed receipts, stale or unauthorized records, prompt tokens and time to first token.

The receipt tells Ada what happened. The profile tells her which test to run. Her merge is still pending. Recovery uses the saved key to find out what happened at the destination and checks current approval for that exact change before any retry.
